text:
sam: Quick check — running into a problem on Next 13 edge runtime where streaming responses hang when the Node/TS SDK is bundled with Vite. Anyone seen this pattern?

jess: Are you shipping the SDK as ESM or CJS in that bundle?

sam: ESM — package.json has "type": "module" and build target es2022. Works fine in Node SSR but edge route starts streaming and then stalls after a few tokens.

ryan: Could be Vite/esbuild optimizing away or transforming the ReadableStream. Vite sometimes turns node-streams into arrays. What does your bundle output look like?

sam: dist/index.mjs — a single file, no externalized deps. I tried adding "browser" field but no dice.

tara: Two quick things we've done before: (1) provide a separate edge entry (exports map) that uses WHATWG ReadableStream friendly codepath, (2) ensure build.target isn't too modern so the runtime doesn't polyfill streams weirdly.

sam: example vite tweak I tried:
```js
// vite.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    target: 'es2020',
    commonjsOptions: { include: [/node_modules/] },
  }
})
```
That reduced some bundling transforms but streaming still flakes.

jess: Check whether Vite is inlining a ponyfill for TextEncoder/Decoder or for streams. Next edge requires native WHATWG streams; if your bundle replaces them, it breaks streaming.

ryan: Another tactic: split SDK into two entry points in package.json exports: main (node) and an "edge" condition. Eg: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs", "edge": "./dist/edge.mjs" } }

tara: Also ensure you're not accidentally bundling global.fetch polyfills for the edge build. Edge has native fetch — polyfills that wrap fetch can break streaming.

sam: Good tip. Our SDK code does a small runtime switch: if (typeof globalThis.ReadableStream !== 'undefined') use edgeStreamPath else nodeStreamPath. But after bundling that check seems to be wrong at runtime (maybe because of shimming).

jess: Try shipping a tiny repro outside Next — plain Vite + static worker with the same bundle. If it reproduces there it's a bundler issue; if not, Next edge could be the culprit.

sam: I'll create a minimal repro and post link. For now I pushed a branch: github.com/rw/repro/edge-stream-repro.

ci-bot: CI passed for branch edge-stream-repro (build #456) :white_check_mark:

tara: I'll take a look at the repro later today. One small packaging example we use in SDK: add an explicit edge entry and avoid transforming streams:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
    "edge": "./dist/edge.mjs"
  }
}
```
And keep edge.mjs tiny — just re-exports the streaming-specific helpers.

ryan: For Vite specifically, setting build.commonjsOptions.include to include node_modules and build.target to es2020 helped us before. Also try disabling minify for a quick check.

sam: Thanks — will try the exports map + smaller edge entry and re-run. I'll also verify Next isn't applying any extra transforms.

jess: Ping @eng-runtime if it still fails after repro — they might know of kernel-level quirks.

sam: Will do. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ryan: :eyes:
